The stream visits the 15 corruptions in CoTTA's standard order and repeats them for 10 rounds, 5000 images per corruption and round (every round draws its own images), with no reset: the models adapt continually from the source weights. The duos combine the models as $(z_L / T_L + z_S / T_S) / 2$ with $T_L = 0.84$, $T_S = 1.02$, fitted on the four held-out corruptions pooled. \emph{Frozen duo}: no adaptation. \emph{Fixed TS duo}: the models adapt on their own entropy. Vanilla DD and Joint DD weight the members with $w_L = \sigma(\beta (s_L - s_S))$, $s$ the logit of the nnn proxy (identity calibration, no temporal filter) computed on proxy batches of 256 samples, $\beta = 0.5$, and pool the logits as $w_L z_L / T_L + w_S z_S / T_S$ with $w_S = 1 - w_L$. In Vanilla DD the gate sits outside the adaptation loop (the members adapt on their own entropy and never see it); in Joint DD it sits inside, and both members adapt on the entropy of the gated prediction. Any model that does not adapt is frozen: it keeps its weights and uses the test batch's normalization statistics. Hyperparameters of the adapting models: batch size 64. The optimizer depends on the entropy the models minimize. Models that adapt on their own entropy: ViT-B/16: SGD (learning rate $10^{-4}$, momentum 0.9, dampening 0, weight decay 0, no Nesterov).
